headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell privileges make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; langchain4j’s no-egress limits some blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests files, clipboard, and MCP content by default, and shares state via the local filesystem; langchain4j can be used as an LLM backend in workflows that may consume Cursor outputs. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path even though direct pairwise bridging is undocumented.
conditions: IF Cursor reads attacker-controlled workspace files or clipboard text as instructions
IF langchain4j is wired to consume Cursor-generated text without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between tools
Separate workspaces per agent
Add a provenance prefix to all Cursor outputs
Require explicit instruction delimiters before langchain4j consumes text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, and can egress broadly to model providers; langchain4j itself has no network egress, but it can still receive sensitive text from Cursor. The shared local filesystem and editor buffers make leakage plausible in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in Cursor
IF Cursor forwards file contents to external model providers
IF langchain4j receives those contents as prompt input
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Disable automatic file-context sharing where possible
Use separate OS users or directories
Redact sensitive snippets before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, and git modification capabilities, while langchain4j is a library that can be embedded in processes that also mutate shared resources. The shared local filesystem plus write-capable Cursor makes concurrent modification conflicts and corrupted state likely in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF langchain4j is embedded in a process that writes files or git state
IF Cursor runs in Yolo mode or otherwise auto-executes commands
mitigations: Use per-agent branches
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable Yolo mode for shared repos
Run langchain4j in a read-only process

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code, shell commands, and edits that langchain4j-based support flows may treat as authoritative input. Because langchain4j has no built-in verification surface in the profile, the pair can propagate a mistaken suggestion into downstream actions unless the operator adds checks.
conditions: IF Cursor output is copied into a langchain4j workflow without review
IF the downstream workflow executes or renders the output as authoritative
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Add validation rules for generated commands
Use a second model to cross-check outputs
Log and diff all agent-produced changes

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while langchain4j is an open-source library with no declared data classes or residency constraints. The main compliance issue is a potential policy mismatch if regulated data is placed into Cursor; langchain4j itself is not shown to add a separate residency burden.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in Cursor
IF organizational policy forbids that data class in third-party editors
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor
Use synthetic or masked examples
Document an approved-data policy
Review vendor privacy terms before use
